summary: This is a sound port of master's proven swap-AB orientation to the router, and no rule is at issue. The expected win is weaker than stated, though. At m<=16 the MMA path is probably not the binding cost, and at m=128/256 the 'weight re-read' is mostly an L2 hit, while the new configs double the fp32 atomic count (SPLIT_K 16->32 at m=128, 8->16 at m=256). Run it once and read it from the router rows' _router_*_kernel times and the prepare() PTX/regs print, not from the headline.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible, but it is a smaller lever than claimed. (1) MMA path. Triton's wgmma lowering needs 64 rows on tl.dot's M per warpgroup. Master's _bf16_swapab_kernel showed that weight[64, BLOCK_K] as the LHS and x^T[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_T] as the RHS emits wgmma with no spills (archive/bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton/1602a4e947e64090.log: wgmma=16, mma.sync=0, 56-96 regs). So the new kernel will very likely move the router at m<=32 from mma.sync to wgmma. At m=128/256, master's router already uses BLOCK_M=64, so it probably already emits wgmma; there the change is about tile shape and traffic, not the MMA path. The print will confirm either way. (2) The router is bandwidth/latency bound, not MMA bound. 8.4 MB of hi+lo at m<=32 is ~0.03 GFLOP. Master's kernel takes 3.2-4.1 us against a 1.8 us floor because each of 128 CTAs streams only 64 KB in 4 short K-steps, plus the fp32 atomics. Swapping mma.sync for wgmma on a [16..32 x 32] tile saves almost nothing when the MMA is not the bottleneck. The m<=16 config, with SPLIT_K 32, K-slice 256 and 2 K-steps holding all 64 KB in flight, is essentially the bytes-in-flight change that router-splitk32-small-m-all-loads-in-flight (1.143x) and its stages3 control (1.152x) already measured flat against 1.151x. Expect m=1/8/16 flat, possibly +0.2-0.4 us from a cheaper register footprint. m=32 is the best small-m candidate, if master's BLOCK_M=32 router tile has high register pressure as the bf16 BLOCK_M=32 tile did (255 regs). (3) m=128/256 traffic. The hypothesis counts 16.8 MB of 'L2/HBM' weight traffic at m=128. But all 128 CTAs are co-resident (128 <= 132 SMs) and the 8.4 MB weight fits easily in the 50 MB L2, so the second M-block's read of a tile is mostly an L2 hit, not HBM. HBM traffic is ~8.4 MB on both sides, and the saving is L2 bandwidth only. Meanwhile the proposed configs raise the atomic count: m=128 goes from 128*256*16 = 524K to 128*256*32 = 1.05M fp32 red ops, and m=256 goes from 256*256*8 = 524K to 256*256*16 = 1.05M. That is 4 MB of reductions into a 128-256 KB output, competing with the L2 bandwidth the change was meant to save. The swap also makes the per-CTA x^T tile 128 tokens wide (32 KB/stage), so x is read 4x (once per W-block) on both sides. Shared memory at m=128 is 3 stages x (16 + 16 + 32 KB) = 192 KB, plus up to 32 KB of convert_layout scratch for the transposed atomic epilogue if it does not alias the dead pipeline buffers. That is close to the 227 KB limit, so the 2-stage OutOfResources fallback is likely to be exercised. (4) Expected directions vs TASK.md: router rows are 62-weight shapes in every load at ~6-9 us of a ~50-60 us load, so a 0.3-1 us router saving is ~0.5-1.5% per load. That is inside the +/-1.5% CI, and the combo run showed byte-identical router rows drifting 0.92-0.94 on verify_1/verify_16. 'flat' for the four bf16 layers is correct by construction. WEAKEST LINK: the m=128/256 'faster' claim rests on removing a re-read that is mostly L2-resident, while the same config doubles the atomic traffic. A secondary weak link is the m<=16 claim, since the MMA instruction is not what bounds a 64 KB-per-CTA, 2-K-step stream.
confounders: router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: this is the kernel being replaced. Its SPLIT_K / atomic_add / torch.zeros design fixes the baseline atomic count (SPLIT_K 16 at m<=128, 8 above). The new configs double SPLIT_K at m=128/256, so any m=128/256 delta mixes orientation and weight re-read with 2x atomics. This is the one material confound.
router-hilo-at-m8: fully superseded on master (the Triton router runs at every m and the fp32 F.linear path is only a fallback). No interaction.
sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: touches only the four bf16 layers on master now. Router graphs are separate per-shape captures. No interaction.

bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo: bf16 layers at m<=16 only, and separate graphs. No interaction with router rows. Its run showed ~6-8% drift on byte-identical router rows, which is a measurement caveat, not a confound.

bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton: the design template (same operand orientation and masked x^T load), but a different kernel, weights and graphs, so it has no runtime interaction. Its success makes the wgmma emission very likely, but it does not show that wgmma helps a bandwidth/latency-bound 8.4 MB router stream.
interference: No companion is warranted under the rule that a companion is needed only when both a gain and a loss would be ambiguous. m<=32 is readable from one run. The prepare() print says whether wgmma replaced mma.sync. The m<=16 grid-depth change (SPLIT_K 16->32, 2 K-steps) was already measured flat by router-splitk32-small-m-all-loads-in-flight and its stages3 control, so a small-m gain is attributable to orientation, and a flat or loss result says orientation does not matter for the router. m=128/256 is readable on a gain (net of doubled atomics, the swap-AB tile pays). A loss there would be ambiguous between the doubled atomic count and the tile change. Since a gain is not ambiguous, the rule does not justify a companion. bf16 checks are spent and every run is a scored submit, so the cheaper fix is a build-time choice, not an extra run. If the implementer wants the m=128/256 rows isolated, give the >32 buckets master's SPLIT_K (m<=128: BLOCK_T 64, grid (2, 4, 16), i.e. master's re-read with no extra atomics; m>128: BLOCK_T 128, grid (2, 4, 8) = 64 CTAs, or BLOCK_T 64, grid (4, 4, 8) = 128 CTAs). That is a design change, not a companion, and it should not go in without the author's agreement because it drops the re-read claim at m=128. Otherwise run as written and judge m=128/256 by the kernel's own top_kernels time against master's 4.9 / 6.9 us, which reproduces within ~1%.
rules_flags: None blocking. hi+lo bf16 split with fp32 accumulation is explicitly allowed at any m. The output is zeroed every call, nothing derived from inputs is cached, and branching is on m (shape) only.

Keep the diagnostic prints (n_regs, n_spills, wgmma/mma.sync counts, including the comparison compile of master's _router_hilo_kernel) in prepare() only, inside try/except, and never print a tensor in kernel_fn. The extra comparison compile of the old kernel counts against the 10-minute run budget (small).
The OutOfResources 3->2 stage step-down must stay a compile-resource fallback recorded as a constant. Never select stages by timing in prepare().

The adapted _router_shape_ok must check k % (BLOCK_K * SPLIT_K) == 0 for the new SPLIT_K (8192 % 4096 == 0 at SPLIT_K 32: fine) and n % 64 == 0. The router tests at m=8 and m=9 (dist outliers) land in the m<=16 bucket. M is do_not_specialize, so the warm-up of each bucket covers them. Warm m=9 explicitly to be safe.
open_questions: Does master's _router_hilo_kernel already emit wgmma at m=128/256 (BLOCK_M=64)? If so, the 'orientation moves the MMA path' story applies only at m<=32, and the m=128/256 rows test re-read vs atomics only. The planned side-by-side print answers this; make sure it covers all four buckets.
What are master's router n_regs at BLOCK_M=32 (m=32 bucket)? If it is near 255 like the bf16 tokens-on-M tile, m=32 is the most likely real gain. If it is modest, expect m=32 flat as well.

Does Triton lower tl.atomic_add on the transposed [64, BLOCK_T] accumulator as vectorized red.global.add (v2/v4.f32, after a coalescing convert_layout) or as scalar strided atomics? Add a red/atom count to the PTX print. Scalar uncoalesced atomics at 1M ops (m=128/256) would likely erase the gain.

Does the m=128 bucket compile at 3 stages (192 KB pipeline + epilogue convert scratch) or fall back to 2? With only 2 K-steps per CTA (K-slice 256 / BLOCK_K 128), 3 stages is moot anyway. Consider num_stages 2 for that bucket by design.

At m=1, BLOCK_T=16 wastes 15/16 of the RHS columns and loads a 16-row masked x^T tile. That is harmless for bandwidth, but confirm the masked load stays cp.async with zero-fill (count cp.async in the print) rather than turning into synchronous loads that stall the wgmma pipeline.
